newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle give Corbidge 400,000 stg pay-off.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle give Corbidge 400,000 stg pay-off.

text.p: British Premier league soccer club Newcastle United Plc joint chief executive Mark Corbidge will receive a 400,000 stg pay-off, after giving up his post, sources close to the company said on Tuesday.

Corbidge, who was only a few months into a three-year contract, joined Newcastle last November, after working for NatWest Markets. He was appointed in the run-up to Newcastle's April stock market flotation.
A club spokesman said Corbidge was leaving by mutual consent after it became apparent that the strategy of employing joint chief executives was not working.
Freddie Fletcher, who had shared the chief executive's role with Corbidge, assumes full control of the post. Fletcher has worked for Newcastle since 1992.
"At the time of Mr Corbidge's appointment it was felt that running the company was best served by joint chief executives focusing on particular areas of the business," said a spokesman for Newcastle.
"Following the flotation it has become apparent that this arrangement was working to the satisfaction of neither party," he added.
Corbidge's responsibilities included group strategy and business development, while Fletcher looked after commercial activities and negotiations with sponsors.
Newcastle shares slipped 2p to 125.5p on Tuesday, some way below their 135p flotation price.
